limitations: The counterexample proves a possible ambiguity for a deterministic stateless predictor receiving only this MAX image and equal effect. It does not show that recurrent agents retaining other history are unable to distinguish the scenarios, nor estimate an Atari frequency or error rate.

An untrained d that differs with order is not a correctly signed/magnitude-calibrated motion field. Nonzero finite P gradients are not useful supervision, stable learning, object binding or accelerated acquisition.
The candidate has no native/archive accuracy test, training run, throughput measurement or gate result. Earlier parser and CPU results remain attributed to their original frozen architecture.

OrderedMotionParser inherits CounterfactualParser, so legacy owners using isinstance may accept its construction even though their pooled-only forward call later fails. Any integration must adapt and validate the new two-RGB contract before a paid command; it is not a drop-in replacement for existing owners/runners.

Source chronology and pixel provenance remain the caller's responsibility. A future protocol must fix the prediction interval and retain the true previous/current pair; the candidate adds no horizon label or guarantee about invisible resets.

The shared pooled feature path still receives P gradients during future learning. Forward independence of f/m/c/s from raw order/effect does not mean their shared parameters would be unaffected by training.

Button-to-effect discovery and the existing motion/foreground self-supervision ambiguities remain unresolved. Small initial displacement does not force nonzero C eligibility; the previous zero-C diagnostics are not repaired or reattributed.
This receipt does not authorize optimizer steps, live integration, new native collection or a modification of frozen sources.
